_comment: Inventory of every event code the core can actually emit from its ROUTED
surface, with provenance. Routing is per-handler: api/index.ts's imports
define reachability, and a handler the router never imports is capability,
Hand-maintained, because ternary and template codes (`ach_transfer.${verb}`)
cannot be resolved by a grep without knowing each value set. Every entry
cites the source line it comes from so a reviewer can check it, and
scripts/build_crosswalk.py --check re-greps the routed surface for literal
codes — both the `code: "..."` object shape and the positional
emit-helper shape, attributed to routed handlers via an intra-module call
closure — and reports any that are missing here.
This file is the denominator of the reachability view. Adding a code here
that the core does not really emit (or emits only from an unrouted
handler) inflates reachability and is exactly the kind of over-claim this

_deliberately_excluded.what: The 83 time-based trigger codes the governance calendar can fire.
why: postCalendarSweep emits String(row.trigger_code) — whatever code a REGISTERED
obligation carries. So the core can technically emit audit.cycle_timer,
Listing them here would move dozens of controls to 'reachable' on the
strength of a CAPABILITY nobody has exercised. Reachability is meant to
answer 'can the core fire this control's trigger', and the honest answer
for an unregistered obligation is no — the machinery exists, the
This is the single largest opportunity in the repo to inflate the coverage
numbers with one JSON edit, which is exactly why it is refused. If these
are ever added it must be driven by what is actually REGISTERED on a real
instance, not by what the code is capable of. See BLUEPRINT 5a.

_deliberately_excluded_unrouted.what: Event codes emitted only by the credit-origination surface, which stays unrouted by the narrow-bank decision (api/index.ts: 'Pynthia is a narrow bank... does not originate credit'): lending.ts, lending_underwriting.ts, collections.ts, the five /fair-lending handlers in deposits_member.ts (postLoCompPlan, postApplicationIntake, postApplicationOptions, postGmiCollection, postNoticeQueue). (The two card-issuance handlers in cards.ts, once listed here, were routed 2026-08-10 — POST /cards and POST /members/{id}/card-reissue — and their emissions moved into literal.) Everything else was routed 2026-08-03 (273 routes) and its emissions moved into literal/templated.
_deliberately_excluded_unrouted.why: Unrouting IS the removal of reachability. These handlers stay for the compliance drill (drill/firers.ts imports them directly to exercise ECOA/Reg B and card controls), but no HTTP request can execute them, so their codes would inflate reachability. If lending is ever routed, its codes belong here from that commit on.
_deliberately_excluded_unrouted.other_unbounded_paths: postCalendarSweep (below) re-emits registered obligation trigger codes; recordMovementArtifacts (api/transfers.ts) re-emits caller-supplied codes — current callers all pass inventoried codes.
